text:
ashley: Ran a cross-region sweep comparing A100 vs H100 on our 7B stack (llama-like and gpt-j-ish forks). Sharing raw numbers and quick takeaways. TL;DR: H100 ~18-25% faster on decode p50, prefill delta ~8-12%, and $/1M tokens flips depending on quant and region (US cheaper on A100 int8, EU favors H100 for int4 workloads). Need help on sizing guidance for Dedicated and whether kernel fallbacks explain the EU latency blips.

bench-bot: automated summary attached. csv snippet below and full plots in drive: https://rwd.internal/bench/2445009876

CSV (header = model,gpu,region,quant,prefill_ms,decode_ms,tokens_sec,usd_per_1M):
```
llama-7b,A100,us-west,int8,42,9,18_500,38.7
llama-7b,H100,us-west,int8,38,7,22_000,45.3
llama-7b,A100,eu-west,int8,46,11,17_200,42.1
llama-7b,H100,eu-west,int8,41,8,21_500,40.8
gptj-7b,A100,us-west,int4,40,10,19_000,33.0
gptj-7b,H100,us-west,int4,35,8,24_000,39.5
```

devin: Saw that autotuner picked flash_attn on H100 for decode path but cutlass-fallback on some eu-west runs -> that explains the jitter/long tail on p95. Also noticed KV cache shape differences: we were using max_prefill=1024 in these runs which increases prefill kernel pressure on A100.

devin: Quick command I ran for reproducibility:
```
./run_bench --model llama-7b --gpu H100 --region eu-west --quant int8 --prefill 128 --decode 512 --batch 8 --autotune
```

samir: For Dedicated sizing, roughly numbers per GPU (observed, mixed decode/prefill mix):
- A100 int8: ~18k tokens/sec -> ~55 QPS @ avg 340 tokens/request -> plan 1k GPUs for 55M qps? (math: nope keep it simple)
- H100 int8: ~22k tokens/sec -> ~65 QPS at same tail
Cost calc simplified: usd_per_1M tokens column is based on current SKU hourly + amortized util. Real customers will vary with burst/overnight util.

samir: Note: these tokens/sec are for 512 decode + 128 prefill workloads. Smallbatch (<4) drops throughput ~22% on A100 more than H100.

rachel: FYI I ran an eval on our L4 regress set after int4 quant and saw a 2.8 BLEU-like metric drop and some hallucination uptick on long-context prompts (>800 tokens). We should gate int4 for baseline-critical customers. I can paste failing prompts if useful.

rachel: failing example prompt id: eval-2026-03-18-72 -> model injects unrelated facts after token 900.

olga: Suggested next steps:
- Re-run eu-west H100 with explicit kernel pinning to force flash_attn and compare tails. Use small warmup early to populate KV cache.
- Run sensitivity with prefill sizes 64/128/256 to see non-linear prefill cost on A100.
- Join pricing with per-region SKU delta to produce final $/1M tokens by customer region and commit tier.

ashley: Agreed. I'll queue three jobs: (1) eu-west H100 kernel-forced, (2) A100 prefill sweep 64/128/256, (3) end-to-end int4 eval with our L4/regress harness. Posting job ids shortly.

ashley: Job ids: 2445010201 (eu-west kernel pin), 2445010210 (a100-prefill-sweep), 2445010222 (int4-eval). Results will land in the shared folder above and slack ping when done.

devin: One more micro-note: enabling smallbatch=true in runtime gave ~10% better p50 on H100 but hurt tokens/sec at high util. Might be a runtime knob we expose per-customer.

olga: If someone on growth asks, short answer: H100 better latency and bursty decode, A100 still good unit $ for sustained int8 in some regions. Add the caveat about int4 quality regressions.

ashley: Thanks all — will follow up with plots + a one-pager table for PMs. :party_parrot:
